text:
alyssa: quick heads-up — ran a novelty-signal sweep on the new Zephyr-13B variants (fp16 / int8 / int4) using the GTN prompt set. summary below, pinging product for routing recs

alyssa: metrics (median over 10k samples):
- fp16: latency 185ms, tokens/M cost $2.6
- int8: latency 140ms, tokens/M cost $1.1
- int4: latency 120ms, tokens/M cost $0.8
- QA F1 vs fp16: int8 -0.6pp, int4 -2.2pp
- Long-context (4k) tail lat 95p: fp16 420ms, int8 370ms, int4 380ms

alyssa: notable: int8 barely loses quality on short QA but int4 shows edge cases on multi-step reasoning and factuality (hallucination rate +3.5%)

marco: thanks. can you drop the novelty signal definition? how are you computing it?

alyssa: simple TF-IDF + embedding drift score across user prompt window (0..1). we bucketed samples: low <0.2, medium 0.2-0.6, high >0.6. performance differences concentrated in high-novelty bucket.

priya: any product-impacting examples? need two concrete prompt failures for GTN to sign off on holdback.

alyssa: posted 3 examples to the shared eval doc (link: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/2745). short: multi-hop math, code refactor task, timeline inference — int4 output dropped a step in reasoning on 2/3.

emily: routing idea: default route low/medium -> int8, high -> fp16, with `fallback=int8` if capacity tight. this keeps most traffic cheap but protects high-novelty cases.

emily: config sketch: ```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"if": "novelty <= 0.6", "model": "zephyr-13b-int8"},
    {"if": "novelty > 0.6", "model": "zephyr-13b-fp16"}
  ],
  "fallback": "zephyr-13b-int8"
}
```

emily: we can attach token budget thresholds so we don't send everything fp16 during bursts.

ryan_ml: will simulate unit economics with current GTN traffic profile. rough calc: moving 25% of traffic to int8 saves ~$0.375/token-M relative to fp16 -> ~30% platform cost reduction for that slice. need to confirm with cost model though.

jorge: can we add a tiny canary: 1% production traffic mirrored to int4 for signal monitoring only? want to detect emergent regressions before rollouts.

priya: product asks for a small safety holdback: 5% canary for int8 routing, 0% for int4 until we fix hallucination pattern. so proposal = emily routing + jorge mirror for int4.

alyssa: agree. ops checklist:
- add novelty detector metric to request logs (field `novelty_score`)
- add per-route quality evals daily (QA F1, hallucination rate)
- canary flags: `route.novelty_policy=gradual-canary-2027`

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout: gradual-canary-2027 created by emily, canary window 7d, initial traffic 1%, ramp to 5% after OK signoff.

marco: one more ask — run these same buckets on the SFT prompt set (edge-case prompt types) and on 8k context benchmark. we should confirm long-context regression isn't worse.

alyssa: on it. I'll post an updated table tomorrow with SFT/8k results and a small sample diff for product.

priya: thanks. once we have the SFT numbers, product + GTN will decide whether to accept the routing policy for rollout.

ryan_ml: i'll attach cost spreadsheet and a quick sim of 3 routing scenarios (all-fp16, default-int8, novelty-routing) to the doc. will include break-even sensitivity to 10-20% traffic shifts.

alyssa: OK team — plan: run SFT+8k, add novelty_score to logs, enable canary mirror for int4, draft routing flag PR for ops. tagging follow-ups: @emily for PR, @ryan_ml for cost sim, @jorge for mirror infra, @priya for product examples. :thumbsup:
